situation (example wording): "What is the current crime rate in Denver?", "Is crime up in Chicago?", "overall crime in Ohio", "most prevalent crimes in Austin", "How does Memphis compare to the nation?"
what the app does today: Each of these words left the question unread (a decline) or asked what was meant.
proposed behavior: Five loose words have one meaning each, for every source. (1) "current" with a figure = the latest complete year. (2) "up" or "down" with no timeframe = the crime named, by year, over the last five complete years (no crime named follows P182). (3) "overall" crime = violent crime plus property crime (P182). (4) "most prevalent" crimes = the seven offenses (murder, rape, robbery, aggravated assault, burglary, larceny-theft, motor vehicle theft) ranked by count for the latest complete year. (5) "compared to the nation" = the place's rates per 100,000 beside the national rates for the same crimes and years. Which other wordings carry the same meaning is decided with Jeff, not added here. Each answer's note says the meaning used (e.g. "Current is read as the latest complete year, 2025."). A question naming its own period or crime keeps what it names.
exact default or choices offered: No question for these words; a question still missing something else asks for that.
why: Jeff 2026-11-21 (through the coordinator): current = latest complete year; up/down with no timeframe = the chosen crime's trend over the last five years by year; overall = violent plus property; most prevalent = the seven offenses ranked for the latest complete year; compared to the nation = the place's rates beside national rates. The reader work is Capability's; labels by rule from question text (Codex second labeler) when the reader PR is up.
test cases: The reader PR's tests; the runner gate lists every question that changes.
